verdict.rationale: Shortwave is an email client, so tracking protection is a fair question, but nothing in the evidence shows it blocks read pixels or remote images, by default or otherwise. On data transparency, the only evidence is community users describing a privacy policy that covers collecting email contents and sharing data with vendors, plus server-side syncing they found uncomfortable. That shows a policy exists, not a product capability that protects the user or explains data handling in-product.

support.subject: As a switcher, the client protects me from senders' tracking — blocking read pixels by default — and is transparent about what it does with my mail data
